title: Drive-and-Kick Passing Lines
description: Drivers attack the lane from the top and kick out to shooters who relocate to open spots, learning the timing of the most common half-court pass.

content.objective: Penetrate to draw the defense and deliver an on-time kick-out to a spaced, relocating shooter.
content.setup: Driver at the top; shooters at both wings; a coach as help defender at the elbow.
content.organization: Driver goes to the wing they passed to; shooter rebounds and joins the driver line.
instructions: The driver attacks the elbow-to-rim gap.
The coach steps in to help.
The wing on that side drifts to the corner; the opposite wing lifts.
The driver kicks out to the open shooter with a one-hand push or pocket pass.
The shooter catches ready and shoots.
coachingPoints: Drive two feet into the lane before passing.
Pass to the shooter's shooting pocket.
Shooters move to the space, not toward the ball.
commonMistakes: Kicking out before the help commits.
Shooters standing still in the driver's line of sight blocked by the help.
Driver jumping in the air without a plan.
content.safety: Coach-helper steps in but does not take contact; shooters rebound their own ball.
progressions: Live help defender and a closing-out defender.
Add an extra pass from the shooter to the next shooter.
regressions: Driver stops with a jump stop before passing.
variations: Drive from the wing and kick to the corner.
Baseline drive and kick to the opposite corner.
successCriteria: Kick-outs arrive on time for a rhythm shot.
Driver passes only after the help commits.
content.gameApplication: Drive-and-kick is the backbone of modern spacing offense.
